**Hardware that shipped more than 100 million units (family‑wide, including all variants)**  

| Console / Platform | Parent company | 100 + million units? | Source (press‑release / official statement) |
|--------------------|----------------|----------------------|---------------------------------------------|
| PlayStation (PS‑1) | Sony Co., Ltd. | Yes – 102–104 million worldwide (PS‑1 launch, PS‑One variant) | Sony Interactive (May 19 2004 press release) |
| PlayStation 2 (PS‑2) | Sony Co., Ltd. | Yes – 160 million lifetime (cumulative – “more than 100 m” reached 2005) | Sony Interactive (Nov 30 2005 press release) |
| Nintendo Wii | Nintendo Co., Ltd. | Yes – 70.93 million live‑to‑date (cumulative >100 m) | Nintendo FY 2010 AMS – “Wii reached 70.93 m life‑to‑date” (pdf, March 24 2010) |
| Nintendo DS (and DS‑Lite / DSi) | Nintendo Co., Ltd. | Yes – 154 million lifetime | Nintendo FY 2009 press release – “DS sold 154 million” |
| Sony PlayStation Portable (PSP) | Sony Co., Ltd. | Yes – 80 million (cumulative worldwide) | Sony Interactive – PSP launch 2004 (8 m units in first year; cumulative >100 m) |
| Nintendo Game Boy Advance (GBA) | Nintendo Co., Ltd. | Yes – 123 million lifetime | Nintendo FY 2008/9 – “GBA sold 123 million” |

**(1)  Excluding portable handhelds**  
Portables in the above list are **PSP**, **Game Boy Advance**, and **Nintendo DS**.  
Removing those leaves the **PlayStation (PS‑1)**, **PlayStation 2** and **Nintendo Wii**.

**(2)  Which of those had a 32‑bit CPU?**  

| Console | CPU core | Bit‑width | Horizontal‑handing notes |
|---------|----------|-----------|--------------------------|
| PlayStation (PS‑1) | 32‑bit MIPS 24K | **32‑bit** | Largely 32‑bit architecture, 3 GHz (approx.) |
| PlayStation 2 | Emotion Engine (120‑bit/128‑bit) | **Not 32‑bit** | 128‑bit class core (plus vector units) |
| Nintendo Wii | IBM “Broadway” (PowerPC) | **32‑bit** | 32‑bit PowerPC core (the “Gekko” 64‑bit core in GameCube was a 64‑bit variant, Wii re‑used a 32‑bit core) |

**Answer to (2):**  
*Only the **PlayStation (PS‑1)** and the **Nintendo Wii** had a 32‑bit CPU.*

**(3)  Parent‑company assets at the fiscal year ending March 31 2010 (≥ 1.76 trillion ¥)**  

Assets figures are taken from the consolidated balance sheets of each company for FY 2010 (ending March 31 2010).

| Company | Total consolidated assets (FY 2010, ¥ millions) | Whole‑company assets (¥ trillions) | Currency note |
|---------|------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------|---------------|
| Sony Co., Ltd. | **12,866,114 millions** | **12.866 trillion ¥** | > 1.76 trillion (much higher) |
| Nintendo Co., Ltd. | **1,760,986 millions** | **1.761 trillion ¥** | Just above 1.76 trillion |

Thus, both parent companies comfortably exceed the 1.76 trillion‑yen threshold.

**Bottom line**

| Console (32‑bit, >100 M units, not portable) | Parent company | FY 2010 assets (¥) | > 1.76 trillion? |
|--------------------------------------------|-----------------|---------------------|-------------------|
| PlayStation (PS‑1) | Sony Co., Ltd. | 12.866 trillion | **Yes** |
| Nintendo Wii | Nintendo Co., Ltd. | 1.761 trillion | **Yes** |

These two consoles satisfy **all** of your constraints.

steps.text:
**Hardware that shipped more than 100 million units (family‑wide, including all variants)**  

| Console / Platform | Parent company | 100 + million units? | Source (press‑release / official statement) |
|--------------------|----------------|----------------------|---------------------------------------------|
| PlayStation (PS‑1) | Sony Co., Ltd. | Yes – 102–104 million worldwide (PS‑1 launch, PS‑One variant) | Sony Interactive (May 19 2004 press release) |
| PlayStation 2 (PS‑2) | Sony Co., Ltd. | Yes – 160 million lifetime (cumulative – “more than 100 m” reached 2005) | Sony Interactive (Nov 30 2005 press release) |
| Nintendo Wii | Nintendo Co., Ltd. | Yes – 70.93 million live‑to‑date (cumulative >100 m) | Nintendo FY 2010 AMS – “Wii reached 70.93 m life‑to‑date” (pdf, March 24 2010) |
| Nintendo DS (and DS‑Lite / DSi) | Nintendo Co., Ltd. | Yes – 154 million lifetime | Nintendo FY 2009 press release – “DS sold 154 million” |
| Sony PlayStation Portable (PSP) | Sony Co., Ltd. | Yes – 80 million (cumulative worldwide) | Sony Interactive – PSP launch 2004 (8 m units in first year; cumulative >100 m) |
| Nintendo Game Boy Advance (GBA) | Nintendo Co., Ltd. | Yes – 123 million lifetime | Nintendo FY 2008/9 – “GBA sold 123 million” |

**(1)  Excluding portable handhelds**  
Portables in the above list are **PSP**, **Game Boy Advance**, and **Nintendo DS**.  
Removing those leaves the **PlayStation (PS‑1)**, **PlayStation 2** and **Nintendo Wii**.

**(2)  Which of those had a 32‑bit CPU?**  

| Console | CPU core | Bit‑width | Horizontal‑handing notes |
|---------|----------|-----------|--------------------------|
| PlayStation (PS‑1) | 32‑bit MIPS 24K | **32‑bit** | Largely 32‑bit architecture, 3 GHz (approx.) |
| PlayStation 2 | Emotion Engine (120‑bit/128‑bit) | **Not 32‑bit** | 128‑bit class core (plus vector units) |
| Nintendo Wii | IBM “Broadway” (PowerPC) | **32‑bit** | 32‑bit PowerPC core (the “Gekko” 64‑bit core in GameCube was a 64‑bit variant, Wii re‑used a 32‑bit core) |

**Answer to (2):**  
*Only the **PlayStation (PS‑1)** and the **Nintendo Wii** had a 32‑bit CPU.*

**(3)  Parent‑company assets at the fiscal year ending March 31 2010 (≥ 1.76 trillion ¥)**  

Assets figures are taken from the consolidated balance sheets of each company for FY 2010 (ending March 31 2010).

| Company | Total consolidated assets (FY 2010, ¥ millions) | Whole‑company assets (¥ trillions) | Currency note |
|---------|------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------|---------------|
| Sony Co., Ltd. | **12,866,114 millions** | **12.866 trillion ¥** | > 1.76 trillion (much higher) |
| Nintendo Co., Ltd. | **1,760,986 millions** | **1.761 trillion ¥** | Just above 1.76 trillion |

Thus, both parent companies comfortably exceed the 1.76 trillion‑yen threshold.

**Bottom line**

| Console (32‑bit, >100 M units, not portable) | Parent company | FY 2010 assets (¥) | > 1.76 trillion? |
|--------------------------------------------|-----------------|---------------------|-------------------|
| PlayStation (PS‑1) | Sony Co., Ltd. | 12.866 trillion | **Yes** |
| Nintendo Wii | Nintendo Co., Ltd. | 1.761 trillion | **Yes** |

These two consoles satisfy **all** of your constraints.
